title: GROOT: Effective Design of Biological Sequences with Limited Experimental Data

problem.claim: Designing discrete, high-dimensional biological sequences requires optimizing expensive black-box functions with limited experimental data.

gap.claim: Existing latent-space optimization methods can produce subpar outputs when the labeled training data is limited.

contributions.claim: GROOT applies graph-based latent smoothing to biological sequence optimization by generating pseudo-labels for neighbors around training latent embeddings and refining them with Label Propagation.
The authors provide theoretical and empirical justification for GROOT's extrapolation and reliability behavior.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report evaluating GROOT on GFP and AAV protein optimization tasks and three tasks with exact oracles from Design-Bench.
The authors report that GROOT equalizes and surpasses existing methods without black-box oracle access or large amounts of labeled data.
The authors report that GROOT can extrapolate beyond the training set while maintaining reliability within an upper bound of expected distances from training regions.

narrative_sequence.summary: Latent space optimization targets expensive black-box objectives in biological sequence design.
Few labeled data points can make the surrogate model ineffective.
GROOT generates neighbor pseudo-labels and smooths them with Label Propagation.
The method is theoretically and empirically justified and evaluated across biological sequence design tasks.
The authors report competitive or superior results without black-box oracle access or extensive labeled data.
